messages:
alex.support: Heads-up — we've got 3 customers this morning reporting intermittent 502/504s and a couple of duplicate-charge reports after upgrading the python SDK to 1.48.x. They all rolled forward around the same time window (02:10-02:40 UTC).

lila.customer: @alex.support here's our trace — requests to /v1/generate succeeded but we saw retries and then a second charge. We didn't change our retries.

lila.customer: paste of headers + trimmed log:
```
2026-03-16T02:14:12Z INFO request id=abc123 status=200 duration=350ms headers={"x-request-id":"r1","idempotency-key":"cust-42"}
2026-03-16T02:14:12Z WARN retrying id=abc123 reason=network error
2026-03-16T02:14:13Z INFO request id=abc124 status=200 duration=360ms headers={"x-request-id":"r2"}
```
We see two successful requests for the same logical operation and both got billed.

alex.support: Thanks. We also have a repro from internal test. Quick summary from initial triage: 1. SDK 1.48 introduced a rename of the idempotency header it sets automatically from `idempotency-key` to `x-idempotency-key` for parity with some other libs. 2. Server-side idempotency lookup still expects `idempotency-key` (legacy). 3. When the server receives the new header it doesn't map it to the existing idempotency cache -> retries from the client are treated as distinct requests -> duplicate processing/billing. 4. Because the SDK retries aggressively by default on some 5xx/network timeouts, this increases apparent latency and duplication.

ben.backend: Confirmed on our side: we only check `idempotency-key` at the ingress cache layer. We didn't add a fallback for `x-idempotency-key`. That explains the duplicates.

priya.eng: Oof. That matches a breaking change we made in the 1.48 PR where we normalized header names. I missed the server compatibility matrix callout.

alex.support: Immediate customer-facing mitigation: advise customers to pin to the last known-good patch of the 1.47 line until we put out a patch. Suggested text: "If you saw duplicate requests or increased retries after upgrading the Python SDK, pin to redwood-sdk==1.47.3 and we'll follow up with a hotfix."

lila.customer: Can you share exact pip command? Also what about existing deployments that auto-upgrade?

alex.support: pip install "redwood-sdk==1.47.3" (or add to requirements.txt / constraints file). For CI/CD: lock file (poetry/Pipfile/pip-compile) update recommended. We'll also publish a security/compatibility advisory for orgs that allow >= semantics.

priya.eng: Action plan from eng:
- Patch server to accept both `idempotency-key` and `x-idempotency-key` (backwards-compatible) — quick deploy.
- Revert the header rename in the 1.48 SDK and cut a 1.48.1 that restores behavior (or better: keep the rename but set both headers for a few releases).
- Add a compatibility test and a checklist entry for any header renames.

ben.backend: I'll put the ingress patch behind a feature flag so we can roll fast and monitor duplicates.

priya.eng: For immediate support responses, use this repro snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="...")
# force the new behavior
resp = client.generate(...)
```
If you want to validate header name in-flight we repro with curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "x-idempotency-key: test-abc" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
You should see the header arrive at the ingress and our logs will show it.

alex.support: Draft customer reply (short): "Thanks — our engineering team identified a regression in 1.48 where the SDK changed the idempotency header name. To avoid duplicate operations, please pin to redwood-sdk==1.47.3. We're working on a hotfix and will notify you when resolved. Apologies for the disruption."

lila.customer: OK pinning now, thanks. We'll report if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment started: ingress-compat-patch v6 -> canary cluster (02:58 UTC)

alex.support: Follow-ups: 1) Priya, can you cut the SDK patch once server patch is validated? 2) I'll open a KB article with the pin instructions and include the repro snippet + suggested monitoring signals (unexpected duplicate x-request-id counts, spike in billing events).

priya.eng: Yep. Will aim for SDK 1.48.1 that either sets both headers or reverts. ETA 6-8h depending on review.

ben.backend: Rolling canary looks clean so far (02:59 UTC). No additional duplicate events in the canary window.

alex.support: Great — I'll escalate to account success for the affected customers and send the advisory. Closing this thread once SDK patch is out.

lila.customer: Thanks team. Appreciate the quick response.
